text: Anthropic just filed to go public. And the paperwork shows exactly where the money is about to move.
The filing went public on October twenty-sixth. The ticker will be A, N, T, on the Nasdaq.
Revenue in twenty twenty-five: about four point six billion dollars. The first six months of this year: sixteen point three billion.
The same six months show an eighty point seven billion dollar loss. But seventy-two billion of it is an accounting charge on convertible notes. Not cash out the door.
No share price is set yet. Reports put the target near two trillion dollars. The last private round: nine hundred sixty-five billion.
So who holds the cheese? Seven co-founders control fifty point one percent of the vote, through a single share.
They have pledged eighty percent of their equity to charity. And a public benefit fund holds five percent of the company.
Then there are the people who built it. About fifty-three hundred employees.
One estimate shared on X puts their stake near three hundred thirty-one billion dollars. About sixty-two million each, on average. That math is not in the filing.
And the landlords. At least one hundred ten billion dollars promised to Amazon, and one hundred fourteen billion to Google, for computing power. Used or not.
The real test comes later, when insiders are allowed to sell. That is when we learn who cashes out, and who believes.
